title: if, else and else if decisions
learningObjectives: Write if, else if and else statements with correct C syntax.
Explain how conditions select one branch of a decision.
Order mutually exclusive and overlapping conditions correctly.
Recognize dangling-else association and use braces for clarity.
Test boundary values for every branch.

understand.concept: The if statement selects a substatement based on a scalar condition: zero is false and nonzero is true. An optional else provides an alternative branch. An else associates with the nearest preceding unmatched if. Braces create compound statements and make branch boundaries explicit, improving correctness and readability.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding if, else and else if decisions helps you reason about program behaviour instead of memorizing syntax. It is useful in exams, debugging and building reliable C applications.
understand.analogy: Treat the concept as a tool with a precise contract: it has valid inputs, defined operations and observable results.
understand.analogyLimit: An analogy is only an aid; the C standard and the relevant function specifications determine actual behaviour.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Basic if

Use `if (condition) { ... }` to execute a block only when the condition is true. A scalar condition is false when it is zero and true when it is nonzero.

## 2. if and else

An else branch runs when the associated if condition is false. Use braces even for short branches so later edits do not accidentally change which statements are controlled.

## 3. else if chains

An else-if chain tests conditions in order. Once a condition is true, its branch executes and the remaining chain is skipped. Put more specific or narrower conditions before broader ones when they overlap.

## 4. Dangling else

In nested if statements, an else associates with the nearest unmatched if. Braces make the intended structure clear and prevent a reader from guessing which if owns the else.

## 5. Test decision boundaries

For a range such as pass >= 50, test 49, 50 and 51. Include invalid inputs and combinations that may overlap. A decision is correct only when every intended case reaches the right branch.

questions.prompt: When does the else branch execute?
options: When its associated if condition is false
Only when the condition is negative
questions.answer: When its associated if condition is false
questions.explanation: else is the alternative branch of its associated if.

questions.prompt: In an else-if chain, what happens after a condition matches?
options: That branch runs and the remaining chain is skipped
questions.answer: That branch runs and the remaining chain is skipped
questions.explanation: An if/else-if chain selects the first true branch.

questions.prompt: Which condition should usually come first when ranges overlap?
options: The more specific or narrower condition
The broadest condition in every case
questions.answer: The more specific or narrower condition
questions.explanation: A broad earlier condition may prevent a narrower branch from being reached.

questions.prompt: To which if does an else associate by default?
options: The first if in the file

questions.prompt: For a rule that passes scores >= 50, which values best test the boundary?
questions.explanation: Testing immediately below, at and above the boundary reveals off-by-one errors.
